topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and mutation progression
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture's learning objectives, the multi-step mutation progression model, and the conceptual framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Deregulated growth signaling pathways in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream intracellular cascades drive sustained proliferative signaling and bypass growth inhibition.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in hematopoietic and epithelial cancers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how genetic disruptions halt terminal differentiation and keep cancer cells in a proliferating progenitor state in leukemias and colorectal carcinoma.

topics.label: Evading apoptosis, replicative immortality, and p53 stress regulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells overcome intrinsic limits on survival and lifespan by evading apoptosis, maintaining telomeres, and altering p53-mediated cell fate decisions.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the metabolic alterations of cancer cells, including aerobic glycolysis, tissue-specific metabolic rewiring, and the role of oncometabolites in driving tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the angiogenic switch, detailing how tumors induce new blood vessel formation to supply oxygen and nutrients required for growth.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dynamics, and genomics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the multi-step metastatic cascade, the mechanical and microenvironmental factors determining metastatic efficiency, and the genomic characteristics of metastatic clones.

topics.label: Lecture summary and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with an overarching summary of cancer hallmarks, recommended literature, and closing administrative remarks.
